question: Should OpenClaw expose Discord bot presence mutation to plugins as a public runtime API, and what gate, account scoping, and precedence model should it use?
rationale: Current main has internal presence mutation paths but no public plugin-runtime Discord presence API, and promoting one changes both the plugin contract and the bot-credential security boundary.

options.title: Design a gated Discord runtime API
options.body: Add a narrow Discord-owned presence runtime seam with explicit gating, account selection, docs, tests, and precedence rules.

options.title: Keep presence as message action only
options.body: Keep dynamic presence limited to the existing default-off `setPresence` message action and document that plugins should not mutate Discord presence directly.

options.title: Fold into self-profile direction
options.body: Defer this issue behind the broader self-profile decision if maintainers want one Discord identity/profile API instead of a separate presence-only plugin API.

recommendation.title: Design a gated Discord runtime API
recommendation.body: Add a narrow Discord-owned presence runtime seam with explicit gating, account selection, docs, tests, and precedence rules.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved decision is primarily whether to add a public plugin runtime seam after the current generic plugin-runtime boundary was established.
